1.
Supplementary affidavit filed today in Court is taken on record.

2. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, Shri Ran Vijay Singh, learned AGA for the State and perused the records.
3.

The present application under Section 438 Cr.P.C. has been filed seeking anticipatory bail apprehending arrest in FIR/Case Crime No.130 of 1995, under Sections 147, 148, 149, 352, 504, 307 IPC, Police Station Gudamba, District Lucknow.

sentences.text: Submission of learned counsel for the applicant is that the applicant is aged about 74 years.

He argues that the applicant was served with bailable warrants in the month of January, 2024 and owing to the age seeks enlargement and benefit of anticipatory bail.
5.
It bears from record that initially the investigation was conducted and the charge-sheet came to be filed.

Subsequently, the applicant approached this Court by filing an application under Section 482 being Criminal Misc. Case No.671 of 2000 in which an interim order staying the proceedings was passed on 30.05.2000.
Subsequently, the said interim order came to an end on 30.04.2013 when the application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. was dismissed by this Court.

6. It also bears from the order-sheet as pleaded in Para 20 of the bail application that the Court below had noticed the fact that the order passed in the application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. was vacated and summons were issued for appearance and on 26.02.2018, bailable warrants were issued against the applicant.

7. It is argued that the summons and the bailable warrants were never served upon the applicant and lastly on 03.02.2024 an order was passed against the applicant and the matter was fixed on 16.03.2024 when for the first time the applicant came to know about the pendency of the proceedings.

8. Learned AGA, on the other hand, opposes the bail application by arguing that during the stage of investigation, proceedings were initiated against the applicant under Section 83 Cr.P.C., and thus,
no case for grant of anticipatory bail is made out, and the same is not maintainable.

He further argues that not only the applicant did not cooperate during trial, he avoided the appearance initially by filing an application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. and even after dismissal of the said application, he did not appear in the trial Court for cooperating with the trial.
9. In the light of the said, it is argued by learned AGA that the anticipatory bail may be denied to the applicant.

10. In rejoinder, learned counsel for the applicant argues that the dispute had emanated from a civil dispute which has been decreed in favour of the applicant in terms of the decree as contained in Annexure - 4.
He, thus, argues that essentially it was a civil dispute.
He further argues that from the side of the applicant also, substantial injuries were received.

He places reliance on the judgment of the Supreme Court in the case of Srikant Upadhyay and Ors. v. State of Bihar & Anr.; 2024 SCC OnLine SC 282 wherein the Supreme Court had the occasion to consider the scope of proceedings before the trial Court when the anticipatory bail application is filed, and the Supreme Court held that there was no bar in initiation of proceedings under Sections 82 & 83 Cr.P.C. merely because an application is pending for grant of anticipatory bail and if an interim order has been passed therein.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 11. It is further argued that the fact that proceedings under Section 83 Cr.P.C. have been initiated was not disclosed when the charge-sheet was filed and the trial Court proceeded to issue summons only.

sentences.text: The fact of the judgment in the case of Srikant Upadhyay (supra) would not be any benefit to the applicant as argued, as in the present case, proceedings under Section 83 Cr.P.C. were initiated at the stage of investigation.

13. The second submission of counsel for the applicant that all the proceedings during investigation ultimately merged in the charge-sheet is prima-facie not acceptable as there is no question of doctrine of merger applicable to the criminal proceedings, starting from investigation and up to filing of the charge-sheet.

14. In sum and substance, in the present case, the applicant continued to not cooperate with the investigating agency, continued to avoid the trial proceedings for as many as 11 years even after dismissal of the application under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
These facts coupled with the fact that the allegations in the FIR are pointing to a grave offence, no case for grant of anticipatory bail is made out.
The present application for anticipatory bail is accordingly rejected.

15. However, the applicant would be at liberty to apply for regular bail which shall be considered in the light of the judgment passed by the Supreme Court in the case of Mahdoom Bava v. Central Bureau of Investigation; Criminal Appeal No.000853 of 2023 (arising out of SLP (Crl.) No.376 of 2023 decided on 20.03.2023 and any other cases which the applicant chooses to rely upon as well as considering the age of applicant being 74 years.
